newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah falls on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah falls on dollar short-covering.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah fell against the dollar in late trading following offshore short-covering in dollars, as swap rates continued to decline, dealers said.
One local bank dealer said some offshore operators were forced to cover their short dollar positions after going short heavily on speculation for a band widening.
He said they were squeezed on declining swap rates.
Swap rates had declined following expectation of ample liquidity on Tuesday after the central bank was estimated to have bought at least $1.1 billion from the market on Friday.
Spot rupiah fell to 2,375/77 at 1015 GMT in London trading, compared with an opening of 2,363.5/64.00.
It closed at 2,366.5/67.0 in Jakarta.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,364.5/65.9 and 2,363.5/64.0, respectively.
"Some players might have been hit hard. It's a decline of some 17 points since the low of 2,359.0 last Friday," one said.
Dealers said there were rumours in the market that the central bank might teach a lesson to speculators by tightening the allocation of central bank papers (SBIs) this week.
"If the rumours come true, people with ample rupiah might be squeezed if they haven't placed their rupiah yet. Interbank rates this morning have given the signals," the dealer said.
He doubted offshore operators had found alternate rupiah investments at present which may result in further roll-overs of existing short dollar positions.
"This is a tug of war. I don't know how long they can hold. They are now being squeezed on the swap side," he added.
Dealers said part of the short dollar operators seemed to have covered because of squeezing in the swap market.
The central bank shrugged off market speculation on its band as it maintained a consistent fixing policy.
Central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said last week the rupiah exchange rate would be kept at a realistic level without anti-export bias.
Some economists said this might signal the band would be kept unchanged for now because a widening would mean further rupiah appreciation against the dollar.
Overnight swap was at 0.05/0.15 and tom/next at -0.3/-0.15.
Swap rates of other maturities fell sharply as well.
They said Wednesday was selected as the day because some players usually went short on dollars on Wednesdays and bought back on Thursdays to enjoy weekend premiums of the rupiah.
One-month swap fell further to 10.0/10.75 from 11.25/11.75, two to 20.0/21.0 from 20.25/22.25, three to 31.25/32.50 from 32.0/33.0 and six to 70.50/72.0 from 71.0/72.0 points.
The central bank defied market speculation and raised its intervention band by one point to 2,364/2,556 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,364/2,412 on Monday.
Dealers in Jakarta said some offshore operators seemed trying to launch another attack on the band by spreading rumours of a band widening on Wednesday.
"I think after what had happened in the market now they would be more cautious to launch such a speculative attack on the central bank," one local bank dealer said.
